memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You saw with your own eyes what the Lord did at Baal Peor. The Lord your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed the Baal of Peor, but all of you who held fast to the Lord your God are still alive today. - Deut 4:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses points to a sobering memory: Baal Peor. There, some of the Israelites had turned to idolatry and immorality, and the consequences were devastating. But those who "held fast to the Lord" were still alive. Moses uses this vivid, recent example to drive home a truth: turning away from God leads to ruin, while clinging to Him leads to life. The people had seen it with their own eyes.

The contrast is stark and instructive. Those who followed the false god perished; those who held fast to the true God lived. This was not arbitrary — it reflected the deep reality that God is the source of life, and turning from Him to idols is turning toward death. Idolatry is not harmless; it is destructive.

The phrase "held fast to the Lord" is worth pausing over. It pictures a firm, clinging, committed relationship with God — not a casual or half-hearted connection, but a wholehearted holding on. Those who clung to God through the temptation at Peor were kept alive. Clinging to the Lord is our safety and our life.

This speaks to us today. We may not bow before carved images, but we face our own temptations to let other things take God's place — to hold fast to money, pleasure, approval, or self. Moses' words call us to hold fast to the Lord above all. Jesus invites us into this same clinging relationship: "Remain in me, and I will remain in you" (John 15:4). Our life and fruitfulness come from holding fast to Him. Let the memory of where idolatry leads strengthen our resolve to cling to the living God, who alone is our life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "idols" tempt you to loosen your grip on God?
2. What does it mean for you to "hold fast to the Lord" in daily life?
3. How does remaining in Christ keep you spiritually alive?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to hold fast to You above all else, refusing the idols that lead to ruin. Keep me clinging to You, remaining in Christ, for You alone are my life. Amen.
